Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

He did not digitize the cassettes, because their cases have a note saying the tape may be fragile. Theo put the transfer logs and the original camera labels in a blue folder beside the tapes. The files are on the archive’s restricted drive, under “Winter Ledger / Rehearsals / 2006.”

I listened to the first three transfer files and checked them against Theo’s logs. The picture and sound are present on all three, but tape two has a brief drop in sound during the scene change after page 31. I can’t tell from that section whether the sound drops on the original tape or only in the transfer. Theo wrote, “The transfer is complete, but the source has a short audio gap.” That is what his log says; it does not establish when the gap began. On tape three, a slate at the start identifies the room as Studio B, while the camera label says Studio A. The room booking sheet lists Studio B for that date, so I think the slate is probably right, but I have not changed the label.

Here is the information I want included with the packet, arranged so Ren can add it to the archive file:

1. The item count should say eighteen MiniDV tapes and four audio cassettes. The MiniDV transfer count is eighteen preservation files, with one transfer log for each tape. The cassette count is not a digitization count; those four items have not been transferred. Please keep that distinction in the inventory, since the current draft says “twenty-two recordings digitized,” which is not accurate.

2. The date range should read September 6–October 19, 2006, with a note that the date for tape seven is uncertain and may be September 16 or September 18. The other dates follow the camera labels and Theo’s logs. I have not verified every date against a rehearsal schedule, so the packet should not describe the full range as independently confirmed.

3. Please list Theo Park as the person who transferred the MiniDV tapes and prepared the logs. He also placed the camera labels and logs in the blue folder. I did not carry out the transfers. Both details are wrong: it is a folder beside the tapes, and the cabinet location is shelf four. The box wording may have come from an older room list, which uses “box” as a general storage term, but there is no separate box with these items. Please correct the draft rather than making a second location entry. The folder and tapes are together now, and I did not move them while checking the first three files.
